Two former Scripps spelling champions teamed up to take first place at the 2026 Adult Spelling Bee in Laredo, a night celebrating literacy and the volunteers who keep it going, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The bee was held at the Falcon Bank Event Center in Laredo and organized by United Way of Laredo through its Volunteers for Literacy program, as part of the weekly “Cuidando Lo Nuestro” community spotlight. William B. Green and the Laredo Morning Times served as title sponsors.

First place went to Missionary Families for Christ: Mary Joy Patricio-Hernandez, Emmanuel Rimocal and Joel Hernandez, Mary Joy's husband. Second place went to the Laredo Public Library team of Danielle Burns, Tori Trujillo and Sarahi Medina, and third place went to Team Villarreal. All participating teams received certificates and gifts, and the top three teams took home trophies.

The winning team brought serious spelling history with it. Mary Joy Patricio-Hernandez won the Scripps Laredo area bee in 2014 as a United Middle School student and represented Laredo at the Scripps National Spelling Bee in Washington, D.C. Emmanuel Rimocal won the area bee as a fourth grader at Kennedy Zapata Elementary in 2017 and again in 2019 at Lamar Bruni Vergara Middle School.

John Maxstadt served as pronouncer, with judges Dr. Laura Ramirez-Cruz, Dr. Antonio Carranza and Dr. Armando Perez, recorder Cecilia Hodges and appeals official Raj Chekuri. Teams from the United Way board, Falcon Bank, Laredo Independent School District, Team Tijerina, “The Bee Keepers” and The Barn also took part. Javier Villarreal and his team from The Barn were eliminated on the word “heraldic.”

Source: Laredo Morning Times, November 8, 2026.

title: Adult Spelling Bee crowns literacy champions in Laredo
